entry.title: PSA Conference — Lukas Stelzl Keynote Talk

link.title: PSA Conference — Lukas Stelzl Keynote Talk

entry.content: Lukas Stelzl gave a talk as keynote speaker about the exciting ongoing work in the lab at the Peptide Self-Assembly (PSA) Conference 2026 in Mainz, Germany (10–12 August 2026). The conference brought together researchers working on self-assembling peptide systems, and Lukas presented our lab’s latest work using molecular simulations to understand peptide and protein self-assembly.

entry.title: GRS: Decoding Disorder by the Numbers — Quantitative and Integrative Approaches to IDPs Across Scales

link.title: GRS: Decoding Disorder by the Numbers — Quantitative and Integrative Approaches to IDPs Across Scales

entry.content: Emanuele Zippo attended the Gordon Research Seminar “Decoding Disorder by the Numbers: Quantitative and Integrative Approaches to IDPs Across Scales” in Les Diablerets, Switzerland (20–21 June 2026). The meeting brought together researchers using quantitative and computational approaches to study intrinsically disordered proteins and was a great opportunity to discuss ongoing research with the IDP community.

entry.title: Hünfeld Workshop
entry.content: Members of the lab attended the Hünfeld Workshop on Computer Simulation and Theory of Macromolecules, held at Hünfeld Monastery in Germany (24–25 April 2026). This year’s meeting marked the workshop’s 25th anniversary, bringing together researchers to discuss recent advances in the theory and application of biomolecular simulations.

entry.title: Girls & Boys Day 2026
entry.content: Our lab once again contributed to Girls & Boys Day. It was great to demonstrate to young minds how molecular dynamics simulations can help us understand cellular processes, using examples of amino acids, peptides, and moving proteins in a box. It was an incredible opportunity to inspire them and show a glimpse of the exciting opportunities in theoretical biophysics.
